product.audience: Young adults choosing a vivid everyday sneaker across street, court and dance contexts
product.decision: Compare three colorways, understand fit and traction, and choose a lace route for a preferred movement style
product.conversion: Create a fictional first-step ticket for the selected sneaker, route and size

signature.moment: A giant sneaker lace path redraws across three pressure zones while the selected colorway cuts into a cinematic moving street portrait

systems.hero: A diagonal triple-exposure street crossing where model feet, vivid sneakers and city light streaks occupy different depth planes
systems.navigation: A narrow pavement-coordinate rail with live route and colorway readout rather than a commerce header or overlay menu
systems.contentDensity: Fast cinematic opening, tactile product evidence, then one focused movement configurator and concise purchase outcome
systems.geometry: Diagonal crosswalks, lace-eyelet arcs, shoe-box lids and outsole tread lanes; no three-column crew stage or lab console
systems.motion: Scroll advances short footfall exposures; choice changes pull an SVG lace path through eyelets and wipe the active colorway into view
systems.coreInteraction: Visitors choose court, dance or all-day movement, colorway and size; the lace path, pressure emphasis, fit copy and ticket update

structuralDifferences: Hero becomes three stacked shoe-box lids opened with explicit step controls instead of a diagonal desktop panorama
Lace route becomes a one-question-at-a-time thumb flow with the shoe diagram above the controls
Colorways use a full-width single pair view with previous and next controls rather than the desktop wall
The final ticket becomes an in-flow box label and size seal, not a group pass, drawer or technical dossier

artDirection.typography: Compressed grotesk display lettering with stencil-like numeric route markers and compact humanist product copy
artDirection.material: Wet asphalt reflections, direct flash, saturated leather and mesh, translucent rubber, pavement paint and corrugated shoe box board
artDirection.imageLogic: Original recurring-model campaign photography supplies energy and scale; original product/macros prove shoe form; SVG handles the live lace path
artDirection.microcopy: Footfall, lace route, toe freedom, heel lock, pivot, grip, colour hit, pair, box label and first step
artDirection.dataHonesty: Fit, traction and pressure values are explicitly illustrative product guidance; pricing, availability and ticket confirmation are fictional

adjacentTemplates.why: Vector is a technical WebGL gait chassis and calibration dossier; AIRPLAY is a photo-led culture campaign whose functional interface redraws a lace route and box label.
LOUDER assembles three people into a shared tee crew; AIRPLAY focuses on one pair, movement route, outsole evidence and size-specific first-step ticket.
AERON uses a long exterior/interior drive film and vehicle trim drawer; AIRPLAY uses short footfall exposures and a direct lace-map configurator.
Motorsport operates a pit-wall strategy simulation; AIRPLAY is a human fashion retail journey with tactile footwear evidence and no telemetry stack.
RIFT develops dark fashion frames and holds one look; AIRPLAY follows ground-level motion, redraws lacing and issues a sneaker-box ticket.

avoid: WebGL exploded shoe anatomy or gait-lab telemetry
Three-person crew mixer, claim tag or contact sheet
Long pinned product film with interchangeable worlds
Generic sneaker cards, carousel-only shopping or side drawer
Robotic models, floating product on empty gradient or giant type covering shoes
Mobile as a compressed desktop page
